methods.name: LIBERO-PeRM
methods.description: A controlled benchmark and procedural generation pipeline for preference learning in embodied agents, built on the LIBERO framework.

methods.name: Vision-Language-Action (VLA)
methods.description: Models driven by multimodal inputs used for generalist robotic manipulation and evaluated on zero-shot personalization.

methods.name: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT)
methods.description: A training technique that makes preferences learnable in policies.

methods.name: Mixed training
methods.description: Training approach that achieves better no-preference retention than sequential adaptation.

methods.name: OMPL planner
methods.description: A heuristic skill library planner used to generate trajectories and perform trajectory smoothing.

datasets.name: LIBERO-SinglePref
datasets.description: A task suite comprising 100 tasks designed to evaluate single-preference learning.

datasets.name: LIBERO-PrefScale
datasets.description: A task suite comprising 100 tasks designed to evaluate scaling across data sizes, tasks, and layouts.

datasets.name: LIBERO-PrefConflict
datasets.description: A task suite comprising 48 tasks designed to evaluate preference-preference and task-preference conflicts.

datasets.name: LIBERO-PrefCompose
datasets.description: A task suite comprising 64 tasks designed to evaluate multi-preference composition.

datasets.name: LIBERO-ComprePref
datasets.description: A task suite designed to evaluate realistic preference-conditioned reasoning based on contextual language.

metrics.name: Preference-satisfaction metrics
metrics.description: Metrics generated by the pipeline to measure how well a policy adheres to user preferences within a trajectory without compromising task success.

metrics.name: Task success
metrics.description: Standard measure of whether a robot completes the nominal task goal.

concepts.name: Motion Preference
concepts.description: A type of preference that constrains the physical properties of the trajectory while preserving task completion, denoted as Pmotion.

concepts.name: Skill Preference
concepts.description: A type of preference that alters the execution behavior of a specific skill c while preserving task completion, denoted as Pskill.

concepts.name: User Profile
concepts.description: A type of preference that uses a user profile or context as background knowledge to guide subtask-level semantic choices, denoted as Pprofile.

concepts.name: Personalized robotic manipulation (PeRM)
concepts.description: Robotic manipulation that requires executing tasks in ways that align with the preferences, habits, and constraints of individual users.

findings.name: Current VLA policies struggle with zero-shot personalization
findings.description: Experiments show that current Vision-Language-Action policies struggle to follow new preferences without preference data.

findings.name: SFT makes preferences learnable
findings.description: Supervised fine-tuning allows embodied agents to successfully learn preferences from demonstrations.

findings.name: Mixed training improves no-preference retention
findings.description: Mixed training achieves better no-preference retention than sequential adaptation, though it can weaken motion-preference learning.
